title: Mars Rover II: rocks and collisions
statement:
Same plateau, rovers and L/R/M commands as Mars Rover. Now there are rocks, given as obstacles, a list of [x, y] cells.

All rovers are on the plateau from the start, and they move one after another. Before each M, check the cell in front. If it is off the plateau, a rock, or occupied by another rover (where that rover is right now), the rover does not move. It stops and ignores the rest of its commands.

Write def solution(spec, obstacles). For each rover return x y H, with STOPPED appended if it stopped. Join the rovers with \n.

examples.why: No rocks, nobody leaves: same answer as the classic kata.
The 4th M would reach y = 6, off the plateau.
It stops in front of the rock.

constraints: 1 ≤ rovers ≤ 1,000; no two rovers start on the same cell
up to 10,000 obstacles, none on a rover's start cell

think.q: Which cells can block a move?
think.a: Three kinds: outside 0..X / 0..Y; any rock; any cell another rover is on right now (rovers that already moved are at their final spot; rovers that haven't moved are at their start).

think.q: Rover A at 0 0 N with MM, rover B at 0 1 E. What happens to A?
think.a: A's first M targets (0, 1), which is B's cell. A stops: 0 0 N STOPPED.

think.q: How would you check "is this cell blocked?" first?
think.a: Loop over every rock and every other rover on every move. That is O(moves × (rocks + rovers)): 100,000 × 11,000 is far too slow.
Hashing: put rock cells in a set of tuples. Keep a second set taken of rover cells. Remove the moving rover from taken before it moves and add its final cell after.

1. Parse all rovers first.
  2. blocked = {tuple(o) for o in obstacles}, taken = {start cells}.
  3. For each rover: discard its start from taken; simulate; on M compute (nx, ny) and stop if out of bounds, in blocked or in taken.
  4. Add the final cell to taken; append the line with or without STOPPED.
Stopping mid-string (later turns must be ignored). A rover blocked by a rover that has not moved yet. A 0 x 0 plateau. Rocks given as lists, not tuples (lists are not hashable: convert).

hints: Convert obstacles to a set of tuples once: {(x, y) for x, y in obstacles}. Lists can't go in a set.
Parse every rover before moving any: rovers that haven't moved still block cells.
Use break to stop processing commands, and remember whether you stopped.
brute:
def solution(spec, obstacles):
    # Re-checks every other rover and every rock with a loop on each move: O(moves x (rovers + rocks))
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in spec.strip().split('\n') if ln.strip()]
    max_x, max_y = map(int, lines[0].split())
    rovers = []
    for i in range(1, len(lines), 2):
        x, y, d = lines[i].split()
        rovers.append([int(x), int(y), d, lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ''])
    order = 'NESW'
    result = []
    for k, r in enumerate(rovers):
        x, y, d, cmds = r
        stopped = False
        for c in cmds:
            if c in 'LR':
                d = order[(order.index(d) + (1 if c == 'R' else 3)) % 4]
                continue
            nx = x + (d == 'E') - (d == 'W')
            ny = y + (d == 'N') - (d == 'S')
            hit = not (0 <= nx <= max_x and 0 <= ny <= max_y)
            for o in obstacles:
                if o[0] == nx and o[1] == ny: hit = True
            for j, other in enumerate(rovers):
                if j != k and other[0] == nx and other[1] == ny: hit = True
            if hit:
                stopped = True
                break
            x, y = nx, ny
        r[0], r[1], r[2] = x, y, d
        result.append('%d %d %s%s' % (x, y, d, ' STOPPED' if stopped else ''))
    return '\n'.join(result)
explain:
The new rules all reduce to one question per move: is the cell in front free? Answer it in O(1) with two sets:

  • blocked: rock cells, fixed.
  • taken: where every rover currently is. Take the moving rover out before it drives and put its final cell back after.

That turns O(moves × things) into O(moves + things). In an interview, extract is_free(x, y) as its own function: the next extension (another kind of blocker) changes only that function.
complexity: O(total commands + rocks + rovers) time, O(rocks + rovers) space

govtech.source: Common follow-up to the GovTech "Roving on Mars" kata
govtech.evidence: GovTech reports name the Mars Rover kata but not its exact extensions; obstacles and rover collisions are the standard second step of this kata in pair-programming rounds.
extensions: Instead of stopping, skip the blocked move and keep going. What changes? (Only the break.)
Report the obstacle that stopped the rover, e.g. 1 0 E STOPPED at 2 0.
Rovers move at the same time, one command per tick. Two rovers aiming for the same cell: who wins? (Define a rule, e.g. lower index.)
Return an error for a spec where two rovers start on the same cell.
